Logs, Activity & Observability ​

Saidi records three separate streams, at three different resolutions, for three different purposes. Knowing which one answers your question saves most of the work.

StreamResolutionWhereRetention
Run thread (RunEvent[])One entry per message, delegation, tool call, resultMongo (run record), mirrored to memory/runs/<id>/run.jsonLife of the run
Raw call log (RawCallLogEntry)One entry per settled LLM call, full prompt and transcriptmemory/runs/<id>/log.jsonForever, never truncated
Activity log (ActivityEvent)One entry per user-visible line across the whole installMongo, memory/activity-log.json as fallback90-day TTL

Plus two ledgers: usageLog on each run (tokens and cost per call) and the org-level credit ledger (money).

The run thread ​

Every run carries an ordered thread of RunEvents. Seven kinds, and no others:

kindWhat it marks
messageA turn of prose — PRIME to you, you to PRIME, or an agent's report
delegationPRIME (or a lead) handing work to a target
questionAn agent asking something it cannot decide
answerThe reply to a question
toolA tool invocation worth showing
resultThe settled outcome of a delegation
systemEngine-authored notices: pauses, credit blocks, branch switches, completion

Each event has id, at (epoch ms), actor, optional to, text, optional detail, optional attachments, byUser, and an optional stats block.

That stats block is where per-message accounting lives:

text
RunEventStats {
  inputTokens          fresh, uncached input tokens
  outputTokens         generated tokens
  cacheReadTokens?     tokens served from the prompt cache
  cacheCreationTokens? tokens written into the prompt cache
  ms?                  wall-clock duration of the call
  contextTokens?       context the session held on its LAST request (input + cache)
  costUsd?             USD at list prices
  costShared?          true when this cost is an apportioned share, not a quoted price
  model?               the model that produced it
}

contextTokens is the number to watch for context pressure — it is occupancy, not consumption, so it does not accumulate the way the token counters do.

See Runs for how the thread relates to participants and branches.

The raw call log ​

The run thread is what a person reads. memory/runs/<id>/log.json is what you read when you need to know exactly what was sent to a model and exactly what came back.

Despite the name it is JSONL — one JSON object per line, appended with a single O_APPEND write per record so concurrent writers cannot interleave. Main-chat turns go to memory/chat/log.json under the pseudo-id chat.

Every record:

FieldMeaning
runIdOwning run, or chat
seqMonotonic per-run index (seeded by counting existing lines on first write)
atISO-8601 completion time
actorPRIME, or the agent/project name
provider / modelProvider and the model string actually used
input{ prompt, systemPrompt, tools, mcpServers, resume } — the full request
output{ messages, finalText, stopReason, messageId } — the full transcript
usageThe RunTokenUsage block for this call
errorPresent only if the call failed
taskId / modeChecklist task and ask | work
effortResolved effort tier
versionOrchestrator build that produced the entry
startedAt / durationMs / durationApiMsEpoch ms start; total wall clock; provider inference time excluding local tool execution
terminalReasonWhy the loop stopped
apiRetries / transientRetry count, and whether the failure was classified transient
unpricedTokens were consumed but the provider quoted no price

durationMs minus durationApiMs is time spent in local tools — the single most useful number when a delegation feels slow but the model is not the bottleneck.

There is no truncation, rotation, or pruning. That is a deliberate contract: a log that clips the interesting part is not a log. The only thing dropped is ephemeral SDK system ticks (thinking_tokens, status), which carry no information and would dominate the file.

Redaction is exact-substring replacement of the resolved values of known secret keys — mongodbUri, anthropicApiKey, anthropicAuthToken, claudeCodeOauthToken, openaiApiKey, saidiGithubToken — each replaced with [REDACTED <key>], plus the Mongo URI password separately. Values shorter than 8 characters are skipped. This is intentionally narrower than the entropy-based redaction used on the activity log: the raw log's job is fidelity.

Nothing in the codebase reads this file back. Inspect it yourself:

bash
# every call in a run, one line each
jq -c '{seq, at, actor, model, durationMs, durationApiMs, terminalReason}' \
  memory/runs/<runId>/log.json

# the full request that produced call #7
jq 'select(.seq == 7) | .input' memory/runs/<runId>/log.json

# calls that consumed tokens but were never priced
jq -c 'select(.unpriced) | {seq, actor, model, usage}' memory/runs/<runId>/log.json

# time spent outside the model, per call
jq -c 'select(.durationApiMs) | {seq, actor, localMs: (.durationMs - .durationApiMs)}' \
  memory/runs/<runId>/log.json

# total tokens by actor
jq -s 'map(select(.usage)) | group_by(.actor)
       | map({actor: .[0].actor,
              input: (map(.usage.inputTokens) | add),
              output: (map(.usage.outputTokens) | add)})' \
  memory/runs/<runId>/log.json

Evidence ​

Verification records what it checked, not just its verdict. A completed task carries an evidenceManifest on its checklist item — stored with the run record, not as a separate file:

text
TaskEvidenceManifest {
  collectedAt       epoch ms
  reportSha256      sha256 of the agent's report, so an edited report is detectable
  artifacts[]       { path, kind: 'run-asset'|'workspace-file', size, sha256 }
  commands[]        { cmd, exitCode, ok, durationMs, outputTail?, cached? }
  provenCriteria[]  criteria a trusted check actually proved
  failedCriteria[]
  changes?          the git delta (below)
}

changes is collected by walking git: { branch, base, commits[{sha, subject}], files[{path, status, additions, deletions}], insertions, deletions }. The base is the nearest proven ancestor among the hint plus staging, develop, main, master (each also tried as origin/<name>) — not whatever HEAD happened to be.

Clipping limits worth knowing, because they change what you see:

  • at most 20 commits (git log -n 20)
  • at most 50 file rows — but insertions and deletions still sum over all files, so the totals and the row list can legitimately disagree
  • at most 200 artifacts hashed; the asset inventory is only built when a task declares an assetCount proof
  • git evidence commands time out at 15 s with a 4 MB output buffer

Artifact paths are validated before hashing: absolute paths, ~, symlinks, non-files and anything escaping the run directory are rejected.

See Plans & Tasks for what turns evidence into a verdict.

Usage and cost ​

Two record types, at two levels.

RunTokenUsage — the per-call measurement:

text
inputTokens          fresh input, excluding cache
cacheReadTokens
cacheCreationTokens
outputTokens
costUsd?             USD at API list prices
unreported?          not one request in this call reported a token

RunUsageEntry extends it and is what lands in run.usageLog, one per settled call: actor, at, models[] (the model it actually ran on first), unpriced?, reportChars? (report length before budget clipping), durationMs?.

The three flags mean three different things, and Saidi keeps them apart on purpose:

  • unreported — the call ran and no request reported any token. Those zeros are the absence of a measurement, not a measurement of zero.
  • unpriced — tokens demonstrably moved but no cost came back. Set when there is no costUsd and either unreported is true or any token counter is above zero. Typical causes: an aborted Anthropic call, or a custom endpoint with no rates configured.
  • costShared — the cost on this message is an apportioned share of a turn the provider billed once, not a price anyone quoted for that message.

Each participant also carries a rolled-up usage, a contextTokens reading, and an unpricedCalls counter, so you can see at a glance which agent's numbers are incomplete.

How a turn's cost is split across messages ​

When a provider bills a turn as a unit and reports no per-message cost, the turn's cost is apportioned across that actor's message events by a token weight:

text
weight = inputTokens
       + cacheReadTokens      * 0.1
       + cacheCreationTokens  * 1.25
       + outputTokens         * 5

The last share absorbs the remainder, so the shares sum to exactly what the turn cost, and every apportioned message is flagged costShared. If the turn was unpriced, or every message already carries a real price, nothing is apportioned. If no message reported usage at all, the whole turn is stamped on the last one rather than smeared.

Read costShared as: this number is honest about being a share. It is not an estimate dressed up as an invoice. See the FAQ for the short version.

Custom endpoints ​

Custom-provider pricing is configured in USD per million tokens, where 0 means unpriced rather than free. A custom endpoint with unset rates therefore produces unpriced entries, not zero-cost ones.

The optimization report ​

When a run settles, it gets a RunOptimizationReport — the run's post-mortem in numbers:

text
generatedAt, durationMs, taskExecutionMs
tasks, firstPassTasks, retries
workMissingFailures, proofFailures, semanticFailures,
environmentFailures, providerFailures
totalCostUsd, totalModelCalls, maxContextTokens

tasks versus firstPassTasks is the honest measure of how well the plan held. taskExecutionMs against durationMs tells you how much of the run was actually work rather than waiting on approvals. The five failure counters are the same TaskFailureKind taxonomy verification uses, so a run whose failures are mostly environment_failure has an infrastructure problem, not a planning one.

The activity log ​

The activity log is the cross-run, cross-channel feed behind the dashboard. It is a Mongo collection with a 90-day TTL — id, t, orgId, actor, msg, detail, channel (main or run), conversationId, byUser, attachments[], and the same stats shape as a run event.

In-memory it is capped: 800 main entries, 200 per run, 1000 recent, 500 sealed, with a 50,000-entry journal. Unlike the raw call log, msg and detail go through entropy-based secret redaction — this stream is displayed, so it is scrubbed harder.

memory/activity-log.json is the local fallback only; in a normal install Mongo holds it.

Inspecting it over HTTP ​

All routers mount under /api.

RouteReturns
GET /api/stateFull dashboard snapshot — runs plus activity
POST /api/state/reloadRe-hydrate stores from Mongo, including activity
GET /api/runsRun list
GET /api/runs/searchRun search
GET /api/runs/:idThe full run record, including thread, usageLog, verificationLog
GET /api/runs/:id/gitBranch, dirty state, commits, changed files
GET /api/runs/:id/git/compare, /git/diff, /git/file, /git/worktreeDiff views
GET /api/runs/:id/files?path=Browse a run directory
GET /api/runs/:id/fs?path=Read a file under the run directory
GET /api/creditsWallet balance and allowance (cloud only)
GET /api/credits/usage?limit=NUsage ledger; limit clamped 1–500, default 250
GET /api/admin/metricsPlatform aggregates over a 30-day window
GET /api/reflexes/logReflex fire log
GET /api/voice/metricsLast 50 voice turns

Two things to note. There is no GET /api/runs/:id/events and no SSE stream — live thread updates arrive over the WebSocket as run_event, run_update and state_dirty frames, and everything else you pull from GET /api/runs/:id. And the raw log.json is reachable only through the file routes above, which cap listings at 500 entries, inline content at 256 KB, and file size at 8 MB.

GET /api/admin/metrics returns orgs, users, liveRuns, creditsCharged30d, rawCost30d, margin30d. rawCost30d is provider cost before margin; creditsCharged30d is what was debited from wallets.

The credit ledger ​

Money is tracked separately from tokens. Each CreditLedgerEntry is id, at, delta (negative for a debit), reason (one of run.usage, chat.usage, topup.manual, adjustment, grant.admin, revoke.admin), plus runId, actor, orgId, userId, rawCostUsd (the raw provider cost before margin), models[], and balanceAfter.

On disk: memory/credits.json and memory/credit-ledger.jsonl. The API and in-memory view keep the most recent 500 entries.

bash
# what a single run cost the wallet
jq -c 'select(.runId == "<runId>") | {at, delta, rawCostUsd, balanceAfter, models}' \
  memory/credit-ledger.jsonl

Because rawCostUsd is recorded alongside delta, the ledger reconciles against the run's own usageLog — if they disagree, the run has unpriced entries. Which limits and caps produce a pause is covered in Settings.
